assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Earth wire
items.clue: The green and yellow striped wire.

items.label: Neutral wire
items.clue: The blue wire, which completes the circuit.

items.label: Live wire
items.clue: The brown wire, which carries the alternating potential difference from the supply.

items.label: Frequency
items.clue: The number of complete cycles of an alternating supply each second, measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.stem: Which statement describes the electricity supply in a UK home?

options.text: An alternating supply, of about 230 V, with a frequency of 50 Hz
A direct supply, of about 230 V, with a frequency of 50 Hz
An alternating supply, of 50 V, at a frequency of 230 Hz
A direct supply, of a steady 230 V, with no frequency

questions.explanation: Mains electricity is an ac supply; in the United Kingdom it has a frequency of 50 Hz and is about 230 V.

questions.stem: Most electrical appliances are connected to the mains using three-core cable. What are the three cores?

options.text: Two live wires together with one neutral wire
The live wire, the neutral wire and the earth wire
The live wire, the neutral wire and a fuse wire
The live wire, the earth wire and a switch

questions.explanation: Three-core cable contains a live wire, a neutral wire and an earth wire.

questions.stem: Two devices are connected across the same 12 V supply. Device X draws a current of 2.0 A and device Y draws a current of 0.50 A. Which statement about the two devices is correct?

options.text: Device X has the greater power, so it transfers more energy overall.
Device X has the greater power, so it transfers more energy each second.
Device Y has the greater power, because it draws the smaller current.
Device Y has the greater power, as a smaller current is much safer.

questions.explanation: P = V I, and X has the larger current at the same pd, so X transfers energy at the greater rate.

questions.stem: An electric kettle is plugged into the mains and switched on. Which statement best describes why the kettle is built as it is?

options.text: It is designed to create new energy from the mains supply that it uses.
It is designed to store the electrical energy the mains delivers.
It is designed to bring about a particular energy transfer.
It is designed to use up the current flowing in from the mains.

questions.explanation: Everyday electrical appliances are designed to bring about energy transfers, here to the thermal store of the water.

options.text: A system of cables alone that links all of the power stations to consumers.
A system of cables and transformers linking power stations to consumers.
A system of power stations that generates all of the energy consumers use.
A system of transformers that increases the energy that is sent to consumers.

questions.explanation: This is the specification's description of the National Grid.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a direct and an alternating potential difference?

options.text: A direct pd stays the same size, but an alternating pd changes size
A direct pd is always low, but an alternating pd is always big
A direct pd acts one way only; an alternating pd keeps reversing
A direct pd comes from the mains; an alternating pd from a cell

questions.explanation: A direct potential difference is always in the same direction; an alternating one repeatedly changes direction.

questions.stem: The insulation on the wires in a three-core cable is colour coded. Which row gives the colours correctly?

options.text: Live brown, neutral blue, earth is plain green
Live blue, neutral brown, earth plain green
Live blue, neutral brown, earth green and yellow stripes
Live brown, neutral blue, earth green and yellow

questions.explanation: The specified colour code: live wire brown, neutral wire blue, earth wire green and yellow stripes.

questions.stem: A potential difference of 12 V drives a current of 0.25 A through a circuit device. What is the power transfer in the device?

options.text: 9 W

questions.explanation: P = V I = 12 x 0.25 = 3.0 W, with pd in volts and current in amperes giving power in watts.

questions.stem: A 2000 W kettle is switched on for 2 minutes. A 100 W lamp is switched on for 1 hour. Which transfers more energy?

options.text: The kettle, because it has the higher power rating of the two appliances.
The kettle, because its rating already gives the energy it transfers.
They are equal, because both of them are supplied by the same mains.
The lamp, because energy transferred depends on the time as well as the power.

questions.explanation: E = P t: 100 W for 3600 s is 360 000 J, while 2000 W for 120 s is only 240 000 J.

questions.stem: Electrical power is transferred from a power station to homes. In which order are transformers used along the way?

options.text: Step-down transformers first, then step-up transformers near the consumers.
Step-up transformers at both ends, to keep the pd high all the way.
Step-up transformers first, then step-down transformers near consumers.
No transformers are needed; the cables carry it straight to homes.

questions.explanation: Step-up transformers raise the pd for the transmission cables; step-down transformers lower it to a much lower value for domestic use.

questions.stem: A student connects an oscilloscope first to a cell and then to a low-voltage supply at mains frequency. Which description of the two traces is correct?

options.text: Both traces are flat lines, but the mains line sits much higher up
The cell gives a flat line; the mains trace crosses zero
The cell trace crosses the zero line; the mains gives a flat line
The cell is flat; the mains trace rises and falls but never crosses zero

questions.explanation: A cell gives a direct pd, drawn as a flat line; the mains pd reverses, so its trace goes above and below zero.

questions.stem: A wire inside a plug is covered in blue insulation. What is the job of this wire?

options.text: It completes the circuit back to the supply
It carries the alternating pd from the supply
It carries current away only if there is a fault
It holds the case of the appliance at 0 V

questions.explanation: Blue is the neutral wire, and the neutral wire completes the circuit.
